result.topic_en: Euler sets the external element forces to zero, introduces end forces E and F on the rod, substitutes these into the equation of motion of the vibrating elastic rod, and differentiates it with ds = dx constant.
result.transcription:
virium exhibet, vis autem nobis per volumen denotatur, formula $\frac{V}{r}$ quatuor dimensiones lineares complecti debet; vnde patet, literam $b$ certam longitudinem referre.

Quia porro virgam a nullis viribus elementaribus vrgeri statuimus, erit tam $P = 0$ quam $Q = 0$. Interim tamen, si sumamus virgam in termino E duas sustinere vires, alteram in directione $EF = E$, alteram vero in directione $Ef = F$. fieri debebit
$\int P\,ds = E$ et $\int Q\,ds = F$.
Cum igitur ob $S = cc$ poni oporteat
$P' = P - \frac{cc}{2g}\left(\frac{ddx}{dt^2}\right) = P$, ob $\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = 0$;
fit $\int P'\,ds = E$; tum vero erit
$Q' = Q - \frac{cc}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right)$, hincque porro
$\int Q'\,ds = F - \frac{cc}{2g}\int ds\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right)$.
His igitur valoribus substitutis aequatio pro motu virgae induet hanc formam:
$Ey - Fx + \frac{cc}{2g}\int dx \int ds\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -\frac{bc^4\,ddy}{ds^2}$.
Pro tensione autem, qua punctum $y$ versus E tenditur, habebimus $-E - \left(\frac{dy}{ds}\right)\int Q'\,ds$, vbi, quia $\frac{dy}{ds}$ quasi euanescit, tensio simpliciter erit $-E$, vnde casu quo $E = 0$ tensio vbique etiam erit nulla.

Differentiemus igitur aequationem pro motu inventam, sumto solo elemento $ds = dx$ constante, fietque
$E\,dy - F\,dx + \frac{cc}{2g}\,ds\int ds\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -\frac{bc^4\,d^3y}{ds^2}$
et per $ds$ diuidendo
$\frac{E\,dy}{ds} - F + \frac{cc}{2g}\int ds\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -\frac{bc^4\,d^3y}{ds^3}$;
haec

items.quote: vnde patet, literam $b$ certam longitudinem referre.
items.english: whence it is clear that the letter b represents a certain length.

items.quote: tensio simpliciter erit $-E$, vnde casu quo $E = 0$ tensio vbique etiam erit nulla.
items.english: the tension will simply be -E, so that in the case E = 0 the tension will also be zero everywhere.

items.quote: Differentiemus igitur aequationem pro motu inventam, sumto solo elemento $ds = dx$ constante
items.english: Let us therefore differentiate the equation found for the motion, taking only the element ds = dx as constant.
